 Dated this the 6th October, 2017  O R D E R P.N.Ravindran, J.
The revision petitioner is the tenant in O.P.(R.C.)No.2 of 2007 on the file of the Rent Control Court,
Haripad, a petition filed by the respondent landlord for an order of eviction under sections 11(2)(b),
11(3) and 11(4)(i) of the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965, hereinafter referred to as the 'Act' for short.
2.

entities.text: Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The landlord had in the petition for eviction averred that he had purchased the petition schedule shop room as per Ext.A2 sale deed dated 22.9.2004, that he had thereafter let it out on a monthly rent of Rs.1,000/- to the tenant for the purpose of running a business in vegetables and that the tenant has kept the rent in arrears from September, 2006 onwards.
He had also averred that he is working in the Pastry Department of a restaurant in Saudi Arabia and he intends to come back and settle down in his home town by starting a bakery business.

He had further averred that he needs the petition schedule shop room to run a bakery, that he has no other suitable building in the locality to run the bakery business, that there are several vacant shop rooms available in Haripad Grama Panchayat for the tenant to shift his business, that the notice issued to the tenant calling upon him to surrender vacant possession of the shop room was returned unserved for the reason that he is working abroad and that he reliably understands that the tenant has sub let the petition schedule shop room to another person without his consent and knowledge.
3. Upon receipt of notice, the tenant filed objections contending inter alia that he has not kept the rent in arrears, that at the time of entrustment in the year 1992 he had paid the sum of Rs.60,000/-
as advance to the then owner, that the landlord had not informed him about the fact that he had purchased the building, that there is no rental agreement between him and the landlord, that the petition schedule shop room is not suitable for conducting a bakery business, that on the immediate northern side of the petition schedule shop room another bakery is being run and that the attempt of the landlord is only to evict him from the petition schedule shop room and to let it out to other persons on enhanced rent.

He further contended that the landlord has got his own shop rooms at Karthikappally, that he is depending for his livelihood on the income derived from the business carried on in the petition schedule shop room and that no other shop rooms are available in the locality to shift his business.

He contended that he has not sub let the petition schedule shop room Sreedharan vs George Kutty on 30 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140421644/
2
as alleged by the landlord and that the need put forward is not bonafide.
He contended that he is entitled to the protection of the second proviso to section 11(3) of the Act.
4. Initially, the tenant was set ex-parte and an ex-parte order of eviction was passed on 29.9.2007.
The tenant thereupon filed I.A.No.553 of 2008 to set aside the ex-parte order of eviction accompanied by I.A.No.554 of 2008 to condone the delay of 154 days in filing the former application.
The Rent Control Court dismissed the said applications by order passed on 31.3.2009.
The tenant thereupon filed R.C.A.Nos.20 and 29 of 2009 on the file of the Court of the Rent Control Appellate Authority, Mavelikkara.
By judgment delivered on 24.2.2010 the Rent Control Appellate Authority allowed the appeals and set aside the ex-parte order of eviction subject to payment of Rs.3,000/- as costs.
Though the landlord filed R.C.R.Nos.145 and 151 of 2010 in this court, they were dismissed by order passed on 18.8.2010.
This court also directed the rent control court to try and dispose of the petition for eviction within four months.

5. Before the Rent Control Court, the brother and power of attorney of the landlord was examined as PW1, two neighbouring shop keepers were examined as Pws.2 and 3, the Tahsildar, Karthikappally who was also the Accommodation Controller was examined as PW4 and the Secretary of the S.N.D.P. Taluk Union, Karkithakappally Taluk was examined as PW5.
The landlord also produced and marked Exts.A1 to A11.
On application filed by the landlord an Advocate Commissioner was appointed to inspect the petition schedule shop room and also to report about the availability of vacant shop rooms in the locality.
The Advocate Commissioner thus appointed was examined as PW6 and the report and mahazar submitted by him were marked as Exts.C1 and C1(a) respectively.

On application filed by the landlord, the register maintained by the Accommodation Controller,
Karthikappally Taluk was produced by PW4 and marked as Ext.X1.
The tenant examined himself as DW1.After considering the rival contentions the rent control court held that the need put forward is bonafide.
The Rent Control Court also held that the landlord has not proved that the tenant has kept the rent in arrears or that he has sub let the petition schedule building to another person.
The Rent Control Court also found that the tenant is not entitled to the benefit of the second proviso to section 11(3) of the Act.

An order of eviction under section 11(3) of the Act was accordingly passed on 29.2.2012 directing the tenant to surrender vacant possession of the petition schedule shop room within three months from the date of the order.
Challenging that order, the tenant filed R.C.A.No.3 of 2012 on the file of the Rent Control Appellate Authority, Mavelikkara.
By judgment delivered on 30.6.2015 the Rent Control Appellate Authority dismissed the appeal.
The tenant has aggrieved thereby, filed this revision petition under section 20 of the Act.

6. The main ground raised in the instant revision petition is that the Rent Control Court and the Appellate Authority erred in passing an order of eviction under section 11(3) of the Act, relying on the testimony tendered by the power of attorney holder of the landlord examined as PW1.
It is contended that as the landlord has not entered the box and has not spoken to the need set out by him, an order of eviction under section 11(3) of the Act could not have been passed.

The tenant also contends that the need put forward is not bonafide, that the landlord has failed to establish his intention to come back and settle in India and that he is entitled to the protection of the second proviso to section 11(3) of the Act.
Sreedharan vs George Kutty on 30 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140421644/
3 7.

After the revision petition was admitted and the respondent landlord entered appearance, he filed I.A.No.2995 of 2015 to reopen the evidence in O.P.(R.C.)No.2 of 2007 and to permit him to examine himself as PW7 and to produce additional evidence.

He had in the affidavit filed in support of the said application averred that as he was employed abroad his brother and power of attorney was prosecuting the case on his behalf on the strength of Ext.A1 power of attorney executed by him on 23.9.2004, that Pws.1 to 6 were examined before he came back to India on 2.2.2012 after resigning his employment abroad, that thereafter his passport was produced and marked as Ext.A11 by consent and that it was on account of the fact that he was employed abroad and came back to India only on 2.2.2012, that he could not enter the box and tender evidence.

He had also averred that arguments in the case were heard by the Rent Control Court on 16.2.2012 and that after arriving in India he has taken a room on rent and is running a bakery therein under the name and style 'A-One Bakery'.
He had along with I.A.No.2995 of 2015 filed an affidavit in lieu of chief examination and produced along with it documents to prove the averments in the said affidavit.
8. The tenant opposed the said application by filing written objections.
He contended that no exceptional circumstances exist so as to warrant reopening of the evidence for the purpose of examining the landlord as PW7.

He contended that from the very fact that Ext.A11 was produced and marked before the Rent Control Court, it is evident that the landlord could have, if he was desirous of doing so, entered the box and testified.
He contended that as the landlord was not denied an opportunity to testify, there is no reason to reopen the evidence.

Relying on Rule 16 of Order XVIII of the Code of Civil Procedure, the tenant contended that the landlord could have requested the Rent Control Court to record his evidence before leaving for his place of employment abroad and therefore for that reason also, the relief prayed for in the application cannot be granted.
9. A Division Bench of this court of which one of us (P.N.Ravindran, J.) was a party, considered I.A.No.2995 of 2015 and allowed it by order passed on 20.11.2015.
This court took note of the fact that when O.P.(RC) No.2 of 2007 was instituted on 17.8.2007 the landlord was admittedly employed abroad.

This court also took note of the contention of the tenant that there is no reason for the landlord to start a bakery business in the petition schedule shop room, that the witnesses on the side of the landlord were examined in the rent control court in November, 2011, that at that point of time the landlord was employed abroad and that he came back to India after resigning his employment only on 2.2.2012, that the evidence on the side of the tenant was recorded in December, 2011, that after his arrival in India the landlord had produced the original of his passport and it was marked by consent as Ext.A11, that it was thereafter that arguments were heard on 16.2.2012 and an order of eviction was passed on 29.2.2012.
This court held that such being the situation, it cannot be said that there was a deliberate omission on the part of the landlord to enter the box and testify.

This court also took note of the fact that the landlord has prayed for reopening the evidence not only for the purpose of entering the box and tendering evidence but also for the purpose of proving a subsequent event, viz. that after arrival in India on 2.2.2012 he has taken a room on rent to run a bakery and is running a bakery under the name and style A-One Bakery.

The relevant portions of the order passed by this court on 20.11.2015 allowing I.A.No.2995 of 2015 are extracted below:
"4. We have considered the submissions made at the Bar by learned counsel on either side.
We have also gone through the pleadings and the materials on record.

The rent Sreedharan vs George Kutty on 30 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140421644/
4 control petition was instituted on 17.08.2007.
Even at that time, the petitioner was employed abroad.
The averments in the rent control petition would establish the said fact.
The tenant does not dispute the fact that even at the time when the rent control petition was filed, the landlord was employed abroad.
The contention of the tenant was that as the landlord is employed abroad, there is no reason for the landlord to start a bakery business in the petition schedule building.
Evidence in the case was recorded in November, 2011.
The landlord was at that point of time employed abroad.
He came back to India only on 02.02.2012.
Evidence on the side of the landlord was closed before that date.
Evidence on the side of the tenant was recorded in December, 2011.
It was thereafter that the landlord came to India on 02.02.2012.
After such arrival, the original of his passport was produced along with an application and it was marked by consent as Ext.A11.
Arguments in the rent control petition were heard on 16.02.2012 and an order of eviction was passed on 29.02.2012.
Such being the situation it cannot be said that there was a deliberate omission on the part of the landlord to enter the box and testify.

The landlord has prayed for reopening the evidence not only for the purpose of entering the box and tendering evidence, but also for the purpose of proving the subsequent event, namely, that after arrival in India, he has started a bakery after taking a room on rent.
He has in the affidavit filed in lieu of chief examination, made the relevant averments in that regard and produced documents to prove the said averments

. Such being the situation, we are of the opinion that notwithstanding the objections raised by the tenant, the application should be allowed and the evidence in the case reopened for the purpose of enabling the landlord to enter the box and tender evidence.
5. We accordingly allow the application and ropen the evidence in O.P.(RC) No.2 of 2007 for the purpose of enabling the landlord to enter the box and tender evidence."
Pursuant thereto, the landlord was examined as PW7 and the documents produced by him along with the proof affidavit were marked as Exts.A12 to A16.
He was also subjected to detailed cross examination by learned counsel for the tenant.
10. We heard Sri S.Sanal Kumar, learned counsel for the revision petitioner and Sri K. Subhash Chandra Bose, learned counsel for the respondent.

Learned counsel for the revision petitioner contended that even going by the evidence tendered by the landlord examined as PW7, the case put forward by him in the petition for eviction has not been established.

Learned counsel contended that the landlord has not proved that he is actually running a bakery business, that the evidence adduced by the landlord will prove that he is running only a catering business and therefore, no reliance can be placed on the testimony tendered by the landlord examined as PW7 or the documents produced and marked as Exts.A12 to A16 to sustain the order of eviction.
Learned counsel contended that even the additional evidence adduced in this court would not justify an order of eviction.

11. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent submitted that the main ground put forward in the revision petition is that the rent control court could not have passed an order of eviction as the landlord has not entered the box and testified.

Learned counsel contended that the main case set out Sreedharan vs George Kutty on 30 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140421644/
5 in the revision petition is that as the landlord has failed to establish his intention to come back to India and to start a bakery business, an order of eviction could not have been passed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the landlord submitted that the evidence now adduced before this court would show that after the landlord came back to India on 2.2.2012, he had taken a room on rent and is running a bakery therein.

Learned counsel contended that in such circumstances, no interference is called for with the order of eviction passed by the Rent Control Court and the judgment delivered by the Rent Control Appellate Authority upholding the order of eviction.
12. We have considered the submissions made at the Bar by learned counsel on both sides.
We have also gone through the pleadings and the materials on record.

As stated by the Division Bench in the order passed on 20.11.2015 on I.A.No.2995 of 2015, the landlord was employed abroad at the time when the rent control petition was instituted on 17.8.2007 and at the time when Pws.1 to 6 were examined in November, 2011 and the evidence on the side of the tenant was recorded in December,
2011.
The landlord came back to India on 2.2.2012, only after evidence in the case was closed.
Thereafter he had produced the original of his passport and it was marked by consent as Ext.A11.
Arguments in the rent control petition were heard on 16.2.2012 and an order of eviction was passed on 29.2.2012.
It cannot therefore be said that there was a deliberate omission on the part of the landlord to enter the box and testify.

The landlord had in I.A.No.2995 of 2015 averred that he has,
after coming back to India, started a bakery business by taking a room on rent.
It was to prove the aforesaid fact as well that he had filed I.A.No.2995 of 2015 to reopen the evidence and to tender evidence.

The landlord has in the proof affidavit filed in lieu of chief examination averred that after he returned to India on 2.2.2012, he had taken a shop room on a monthly rent of Rs.1,750/- and that the rent was later enhanced to Rs.2,250/- per mensem.

He had also produced and marked the licence issued by Chingoli Grama Panchayat for running a borma (oven) in a portion of his house as Ext.A13, the registration certificates issued by the Food Safety Officer, Haripad under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 as Exts.A14 and A15 in respect of the borma and the bakery and the licence issued by the Karthikappally Panchayat to run the bakery in tenanted premises as Ext.A16.
13.
The evidence adduced by the landlord in this court would show that he had, after coming back to India on 2.2.2012, taken a building on rent and is running a bakery business therein.
Exts.A12 and A16 establish the said fact.

Exts.A13 and A14 also prove that he is running a borma in a portion of his residential house, after obtaining the requisite licence from Chingoli Grama Panchayat and registration under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
It has also come out in evidence that his residence is situate within the local limits of Chingoli Grama Panchayat and that in a portion of it a borma has been erected.
It has also come out in evidence that the shop room in which the bakery is being run, is in Karthikappally Panchayat and it is about two furlongs away from his residence.
Though
the landlord was cross examined at length, nothing was brought out to discredit his testimony.

The evidence tendered by the landlord in this court establishes beyond doubt that after coming back to India on 2.2.2012 he has started a bakery and is running it after obtaining the requisite licence.
The fact that he is running the bakery in tenanted premises, is also adequately proved.
14. In the light of the overwhelming evidence on record, it cannot be said that the need put forward is only a ruse to evict the tenant.

The landlord has, as a matter of fact, come back to India after Sreedharan vs George Kutty on 30 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140421644/
6 resigning his employment abroad and is running a bakery in a rented building.
The tenant cannot therefore contend that the need is not bonafide and is only a ruse to evict him.
The tenant cannot also contend that the landlord who is running the bakery in a tenanted premises, should not evict him for the purpose of running his business in his own building.
In such circumstances, we are satisfied that no exception can be taken to the order of eviction passed by the Rent Control Court and affirmed by the Rent Control Appellate Authority.
We accordingly hold that there is no merit in the instant revision petition.
The revision petition fails and is accordingly dismissed.

However, having regard to the fact that the tenant has been running a business in the tenanted premises for the past several years, we deem it appropriate to grant him three months time from today to surrender vacant possession of the petition schedule building subject to the condition that he shall, within two weeks from today, file an undertaking in the form of an affidavit in the Rent Control Court undertaking to surrender vacant possession of the petition schedule building to the landlord on the expiry of the said period of three months.

He shall further undertake in the said affidavit that he will not induct third parties into possession of the petition schedule building and that he will not sub let it or commit acts of waste therein.
He shall also deposit on the day the affidavit is filed, the arrears of rent, if any, and undertake in the affidavit that he will continue to pay rent at the contract rate till the date of surrender.

(P.N. Ravindran, Judge) (K.Ramakrishnan, Judge) kav/
